# SESAME

> SESAME is Wayne State's protocol-neutral auth library for PHP: a verified identity for your app, app-native sessions, and drivers behind one config switch. Raw PHP, Laravel/Blade and Inertia/Vue.

**The way in. One lock, any key.** Single Entry, Sessions App-Managed Everywhere: keys cut while you wait, and no
key ever gets to keep the door.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub). Both pipelines run the same five checks (manifest, tests, Pint, PHPStan, audit), so a green build means the same thing on both sides.

Our CI is the same script on both sides, so when it fails, nobody gets to blame the other platform.

SESAME is Wayne State's protocol-neutral auth library. It returns a verified
identity and leaves the session to the app: every driver ends in the same
place, the app's `findOrImportUser(Identity)`, and the protocol never holds
the session. Switching driver is a config change with no code change. Open
sesame.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page you can open in a browser or serve from `site/`.
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

This repository is published from Wayne State University's internal GitLab and
mirrored here. Changes land there first; Wayne State developers open issues
and merge requests on the internal project.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [SESAME: The way in.](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): SESAME is Wayne State's protocol-neutral auth library for PHP: a verified identity for your app, app-native sessions, and drivers behind one config switch. Raw PHP, Laravel/Blade and Inertia/Vue.

## Prompts

- [Get started with SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): Which doorway the app is, which key it needs, and the smallest plan to sign people in with a verified identity. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [SESAME in a raw PHP app](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): The core wired by hand: config, the driver, a user resolver, the app's own session, and a logout that only a POST can ring. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [SESAME in a Laravel app with Blade](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-blade): The adapter the Laravel way: published config, a user resolver, the auth.sesame middleware and a CSRF-guarded sign-out. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [SESAME in a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-inertia): The same adapter. The middleware guards each route before any Vue page is sent, and the user reaches Vue as a prop. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Move a Laravel app from wayne-cas to SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-wayne-cas): The shim keeps the old names, so the move is a mapping, not a rewrite. The agent lists every part before it swaps one. The prompt itself is in https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
